source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 36 MW of IT load across three buildings, and its certifications point to finance, healthcare, and federal tenants rather than AI training.

The campus holds PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 certifications. Those are credentials for regulated workloads, which need compliance and redundancy more than the rack density that AI training clusters demand. The published 296,000 square feet of technical space, read at a common 40 kW per rack for AI training, works out to roughly 900 racks. That density suggests the 36 MW figure describes the current footprint rather than a future buildout.

Texas is a state where disclosure is the exception. Only 19 of 133 mapped facilities publish capacity figures, and the published total is 475 MW. This campus ranks fourth in the state at 7.6% of that total. The rank measures how few operators publish specifications, not how important the site is to AI scaling.

What the data does not cover matters here. The grid constraint and power availability for this site are not published, so nothing here speaks to whether the campus can actually be served at higher load. Announced expansion is also absent, and the suitability score of 68 is computed from published IT capacity and operator type alone, with expansion listed as a missing input.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
